In support of this suggestion, many factors relating to the spillover of industrial development and population growth from Dade into Broward were cited. These are certainly relevant factors, but we do not feel that areas as far as 55 miles from the Miami corporate limits can be considered "adjacent to" the base municipality. As previously explained, the meaning of "adjacent" is not static, but at this time we believe the formula distances adopted generally correspond to a reasonable conception of the term based on current economic and technological conditions and the extent of local transportation systems.
The available economic evidence buttresses our belief that the parameters of the population-mileage formula adopted herein provide a reasonable approximation of the extent of modern urban area commercial development. Subsequent to the issuance of the Interim Report, this Commission's Bureau of Economics undertook an independent economic evaluation of the population-mileage formula proposed herein. This in-depth study considered the detailed economic analysis presented by the Freight Forwarders Institute, the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, the Short Haul Survival Committee and others. The Bureau also conducted an extensive survey of representative municipalities in each population category of the formula. The results of this evaluation and survey are contained in a report prepared by the Bureau and reproduced in Appendix B. The findings of the Bureau bear out the conclusions reached both here and in the Interim Report with respect to the proper parameters of the population-mileage formula.
